subject: dur_day_spt_min not equal to 1440 min (in midnight-midnight reports)

messages.author: 6ce96e3e4a314db1
messages.subject: dur_day_spt_min not equal to 1440 min (in midnight-midnight reports)
parts:
Hello,

I am new to GGIR and have encountered an issue that seems to be similar to what others have reported recently in this group. I’m hoping someone can provide some clarity on the matter.

We are using GGIR package version 3.2 to analyze accelerometer data from Actigraph GT3X-BT devices. Study participants have been instructed to wear the accelerometer on their non-dominant wrist for 3 weeks, 24/7, only taking it off during water-based activities.

In both the cleaned daysummary (part5_daysummary_MM_L44.8M100.6V428.8_T5A5) and full daysummay report (part5_daysummary_full_MM_L44.8M100.6V428.8_T5A5), we have observed unexpected values for the dur_day_spt_min variable. Since we are working with midnight-to-midnight reports, we would expect all values for dur_day_spt_min to be 1440 minutes (24 hours). Although most of the full windows in our output files are 1440 minutes, some deviate in both the cleaned and full daysummary.

Specifically, 14 of the days present in part5_daysummary_MM_L44.8M100.6V428.8_T5A5 are longer than 1440 minutes (ranging from 1500 to 3720 minutes). Additionally, three days show durations shorter than expected (each is 1380 minutes). The report contains nearly 900 days, so this issue does not occur for every participant. Furthermore, it tends to affect the first or last window of the measurement period.

I have attached the script we have been using for reference.

We are unsure how to interpret these results or whether something went wrong during the analysis. Any advice on this issue would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you in advance!

Emilia

Hi Vincent,

Thank you for your reply.

The previous posts I was referring to are:

  • https://groups.google.com/g/RpackageGGIR/c/3mTxbliFoyc/m/PSXk5P8ZBAAJ

  • https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/0nvXVHcCVUU/m/-IiBQMAfCAAJ

I noticed your response to the first post, where you mentioned that the values of the dur_day_spt_min_pla variable can exceed 1440 minutes if they are derived from the WW-report. However, I find it interesting that I observe similarly high durations even when analyzing the MM-reports.

Unfortunately, I am unable to share example data due to data protection regulations, so I understand that it might be difficult to investigate the issue I am encountering. That said, since I have observed this behavior across all batches of my data, I wanted to check whether there might be an obvious oversight in my analysis or potentially a bug in GGIR contributing to this.

Kind regards,
Emilia
